key_insight: A unified statistical framework combines passage-level signals to audit whether individual documents or collections were used to train an LLM.
clinical_relevance: For medical LLMs, the framework could support privacy and benchmark-contamination audits by assessing whether medical question-answer records were used in training.
method: Combine complementary chunk-level membership evidence using Cauchy combination to score documents.
Calibrate document-level p-values and aggregate evidence for collection-wide auditing.
Use multiple testing to identify suspicious documents with false discovery rate control.
evidence_signal: Case studies on BookTection, Pile-arXiv, Cosmopedia, and HealthCareMagic evaluated pre-training and fine-tuning audits; the abstract reports effectiveness and reliability without numerical results.
watch_item: Statistical error-control guarantees depend on the stated exchangeability conditions, which require scrutiny in real-world audits.
paper_title: A Statistical Framework for Training Data Auditing of Large Language Models
